meta.topic: Interrogation regarding the theft of the 'Star of Midnight' diamond.

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: Julian Vance, I've reviewed your alibi for the time of the theft - a dinner party at a friend's residence, supposedly from 18:00 to 22:00. Can you confirm that you left the party at 21:30 and walked home, as you claimed?

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I recall the evening quite clearly, and I left my friend's residence around 21:45 to take a short walk, which should have been long enough to cover the distance to the Grand Bistro. I then arrived around 21:50 and had dinner at 21:55, as I had reservations.

{"confessed": false}

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: Your walk should have taken approximately 15 minutes, yet you claim to have arrived at the Grand Bistro around 21:50. Did you actually stop for a drink or conversation at the bistro at 21:50, or did you simply walk past it?

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I may have been a bit rushed, but I did indeed stop for a drink at the bistro around 21:50, and I recall having a brief conversation with the bartender. I recall the conversation quite vividly, as it was with a friend of mine who was also a patron.

{"confessed": false}

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: Your friend, you say? Yet, when I spoke with your acquaintances, they reported that you were alone during that time, and none of them saw you with a friend at the bistro. Can you explain this discrepancy?

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I must have misspoken earlier. I was indeed alone at the bistro, and I must have gotten carried away with the conversation. I don't recall having a conversation with a friend, but I do remember enjoying a fine glass of wine and savoring the meal.

{"confessed": false}

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: A fine glass of wine and a meal, you say? I've reviewed the bistro's security footage, and it shows you arriving at 21:50, but leaving around 22:20. Can you account for the two-and-a-half-hour gap during which time you claim to have been alone and enjoying your meal?

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I must have lost track of time, it's not uncommon for me to get engrossed in a good book or a fascinating conversation. I'm pretty sure I took a short walk outside to clear my head around 22:00, and then returned to my table for dessert, which would explain the 20-minute gap.

{"confessed": false}

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: A short walk outside, you say? I've spoken to the bistro staff, and they reported that during that time, the restaurant was relatively quiet, with only a handful of patrons. They didn't notice you taking a walk, but they did see one person leaving around 22:10 - a man who matched your description, wearing a dark coat and a hat.

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I'm not surprised the staff didn't notice me taking a walk, as I did try to be discreet. As for the man leaving around 22:10, I'm quite certain he was a delivery person or a waiter, and I think I might have mistaken him for someone else. I've been to this bistro many times, and the staff can be quite familiar with my face.

{"confessed": false}

messages.speaker: Detective Cross
messages.content: I see you're quite confident in your identification of the man. However, I've reviewed the bistro's security footage, and it appears the man who left around 22:10 was actually wearing a distinctive gold watch that you don't own. Can you explain why you own a watch that you wouldn't normally wear?

messages.speaker: Julian Vance
messages.content:
I may have acquired a new watch recently as a gift from a friend, and I sometimes wear it to the bistro when I'm out for dinner. It's not a common accessory, but I suppose I was wearing it that evening.

{"confessed": false}
